ORDER The civil miscellaneous petition is filed to condone the delay of 3526 days in re-presenting the returned papers for filing the civil miscellaneous appeal.
2. It is the case of the petitioner that challenging the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, he filed the present appeal with a delay of 693 days.

It is averred in the affidavit filed in support of the petition that the appeal papers were returned by the Registry and the previous counsel misplaced the papers and therefore it was not re-presented within the time.

It is further averred in the affidavit that, when the petitioner enquired about the status of the case in the year https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 2020, the previous counsel informed that he would take necessary steps to number the appeal.
Later, during January 2024, the counsel traced out the the old case bundle and handed over the same to the petitioner.
After collecting the returned papers from the previous counsel, the petitioner engaged the present counsel for re-presenting the papers with a delay of 3526 days in re-presenting the papers.
3. As per the averments found in the affidavit of the petitioner, the civil miscellaneous papers were presented before this court on 10.04.2014.
However, the petitioner has not taken any steps to enquire about the status of the case nearly for six years.
Even as per the averment made in the affidavit, the petitioner approached the counsel only in the year 2020.
Absolutely, there is no reason for condoning such inordinate delay of six years in making enquiry about the status of the appeal papers.
Therefore, the petitioner failed to explain the reasons for the inordinate delay of 3526 days in re-presenting the returned papers and hence, this court is not inclined to entertain this petition.
4. Accordingly, this civil miscellaneous petition is dismissed.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
Consequently, the civil miscellaneous appeal is rejected at the SR stage itself.
There shall be no order as to costs.
